In this module we will go deeper into our exploration of raster data! You will learn new tools for working with raster data and conduct point pattern analyses. Specifically, you will learn how to:

-   Convert rasters to shapefiles
-   Change raster resolution via resampling
-   Sample a raster to generate points within a raster
-   Calculate spatial density using rasters
-   Generate distance rasters
-   How to identify, address, and use, spatial autocorrelation in your data

## Module overview

* **7.1 Advanced rasters**: This video (runtime: 36:40) and written lesson covers how to convert rasters to shapefiles, change raster resolution, calculate distance and density, calculate terrain information from rasters (e.g., slope), and sample rasters in new ways.
* **7.2 Spatial autocorrelation ... and more**: In this video lesson (runtime: 49:28) you will learn about the super important concept of spatial autocorrelation and how to apply the concept to study design and generating useful continuous surfaces (rasters) from point data. Please note that you will not be evaluated on the majority of this lesson (see lesson overview).

**Problem Set** (due 12 Oct): A mountain holiday for Tara

## Getting started

Please complete the following steps *prior* to beginning this week's lessons:

* Download `module_7_files.zip` and:
    * Place the folder `gis_scbi` inside of the `data/raw` folder
    * Place any remaining `*.rds` or `*.csv` files inside of the `data/raw` folder
    * Place any remaining `*.geojson` files inside of the `data/raw/shapefiles` folder
    * Place any remaining `*.tif` files inside of the `data/raw/rasters` folder
    * Place any R script files ([*.R]) inside of the `scripts` folder
* Run the following to install several new packages!

```{r}
#| eval: false

install.packages(
  c(
    "ape",
    "gstat",
    "pgirmess",
    "spatstat"
  )
)
```

***Important!***: *terra* will attempt to temporarily store raster files in your computer's memory. If it is unable to do so, it will store the data as a hidden temporary file on your hard drive Be sure to clear up enough space in your hard disk (at least 5 GB) to complete *terra* operations. If it is unable to store the file, you will get a very vague message about running out of memory (but this message actually has to do with running of hard disk space).
